gen_risks.description: Limited market demand for sustainable finance instruments may result in low uptake of SLLs and GLs by SMEs and mid‑caps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement aggressive outreach, incentives, and pilot programmes; work with anchor firms to create pipeline of eligible projects.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 7: market for sustainable finance instruments remains nascent and concentrated among large corporations.

gen_risks.description: Credit risk of beneficiary enterprises could lead to loan defaults, especially under climate‑related stress.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply rigorous credit underwriting, require co‑financing, embed climate‑risk assessments, and price risk premiums accordingly.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 30: NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs; Section 19: extreme temperatures raise loan delinquency rates.

gen_risks.description: Participating financial institutions lack capacity to design, appraise and monitor green loans, risking poor loan quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver targeted technical assistance, training, and standardized appraisal tools to PFIs before and during rollout.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 15: limited capacity of Mexican financial institutions to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) systems could impede tracking of emissions and sustainability performance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop standardized MRV templates, fund independent validation, and embed MRV requirements in loan agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 15: limited availability of credible MRV systems constrains lenders’ ability to evaluate environmental performance.

gen_risks.description: Gender gap in access to finance may limit participation of women‑owned firms, reducing intended inclusive outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set explicit women‑inclusive eligibility criteria, run gender‑focused outreach, and monitor women‑led beneficiary numbers.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 20/46: women‑owned firms have lower credit access; project will track women‑led businesses.

gen_risks.description: Delays in finalising the Project Operations Manual and Sustainable Finance Framework could postpone implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare draft documents early, secure stakeholder review, and align with Bank standards to meet effectiveness conditions.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 29: POM approval is a condition of loan effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Disbursement caps on retroactive financing may restrict early‑stage payments, causing cash‑flow bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Schedule expenditures to fit within approved caps, use advance method where allowed, and submit supporting documentation promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 42‑44: retroactive financing limited to US$40 M (IBRD), US$9.92 M (CCEFCF), US$0.8 M (ESMAP).

gen_risks.description: Second‑tier PFIs may underperform or delay on‑lending, limiting SME access to finance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include performance‑based covenants, regular monitoring, and fallback mechanisms to re‑allocate funds to alternative PFIs.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 30‑31: PFIs assume credit risk and are responsible for on‑lending to BEs.

gen_risks.description: Risk of greenwashing if sustainability targets are not independently verified.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification by qualified independent entities for all SLL/GL projects.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 61: ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification to mitigate greenwashing risk.

gen_risks.description: Physical climate hazards (heatwaves, floods) could impair beneficiary operations and loan repayment ability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑risk assessments into loan appraisal, promote resilience‑enhancing technologies, and consider climate insurance where feasible.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 19: climate events increase operational costs and loan delinquency among Mexican firms.

gen_risks.description: NAFIN’s limited experience in direct procurement may cause procedural errors or delays for Component 2 contracts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a qualified internal procurement professional and provide hands‑on Bank training and supervision during early procurements.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 57‑58: NAFIN staff not previously involved in procurement; mitigation plan outlined.

gen_risks.description: Residual fiduciary risk from reliance on legacy financial systems could affect accurate recording and reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen reconciliation procedures, conduct targeted internal audits, and enforce three‑lines‑of‑defense control model.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 54: residual FM risk assessed as Moderate due to legacy systems.

gen_risks.description: Currency fluctuations between MXN and USD may increase borrowing costs for firms with USD‑denominated loans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Limit USD exposure, use Mexico’s currency‑swap market for hedging, and match loan currency to borrower’s natural hedge.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 31: financing mostly in local currency; NAFIN will manage FX risk via swaps.

gen_risks.description: Future changes to Mexico’s Sustainable Taxonomy or related regulations could render eligibility criteria obsolete.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor policy developments, design eligibility criteria with flexibility, and maintain a rapid amendment process for the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 7‑9: taxonomy guides eligibility; government may adjust policies.

gen_risks.description: Target of mobilising US$89 M private capital may not be achieved, reducing overall leverage effect.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement proactive investor outreach, showcase pilot successes, and consider partial credit guarantees to de‑risk private participation.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 28‑29: aim to mobilise US$89 M private capital; reliance on co‑financing.

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
